subject: LaunchDarkly contract renewal — cost / SLO / export tradeoffs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@launchdarkly.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Contract up for renewal — need detailed options

Hi Sarah,

Our LaunchDarkly agreement is up for renewal 2026-12-31 and I wanted to start a quick thread to gather options. We’re evaluating whether to: (a) renew with a 12 month term, (b) sign a longer commit for better economics, or (c) plan for a partial migration of non-critical services to an OSS flagging alternative.

To make a decision we need the following from you by end of next week:
- Itemized pricing for both 12-month and 36-month commitments (including any seat / MAU thresholds and overage formulas)
- Any available cap/guardrails for monthly active flags / targets we can set to control cost
- Exportable audit logs and the format/frequency (we need full event history exports for compliance)
- Details on on-prem / VPC SDK support and signing keys management (we have regulated workloads)
- Current SLA / SLO language and remedies for downtime or degraded SDK performance

Attached is our rough usage report for Oct-Nov to help size the ask (usage_report_oct_nov.csv).

Cc’ing Laura and David to flag finance / legal constraints up front: we want to avoid a large price step up without commensurate reliability or exportability guarantees. Ava and Marissa are pulled in for engineering impact.

Thanks — can you confirm you’ve received and when we can expect the detailed proposal?

Best,
Karthik
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@launchdarkly.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@launchdarkly.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract up for renewal — need detailed options

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the heads up — appreciate the usage file, that helps. I’ve put together a draft proposal (LD_proposal_Q4_2026.pdf) that outlines both 12- and 36-month pricing tiers, and a few add-ons (priority support, SLA uplift, and an export API for audit logs). High level: with a 36-month commit we can offer up to a 22% discount vs list; 12-month renewals will be ~10% uplift on current pricing due to product changes and SDK improvements.

On your specific asks:
- Caps on MAUs/flags: we can set guardrails and notification thresholds, but true hard caps are not part of the standard product — we can discuss a contractual cap for an enterprise addendum.
- Exports: we offer a daily export feed (CSV/JSON) of audit events; full historical exports can be delivered on request for migration, timeline depends on volume.
- On-prem / VPC: we have a private deployment option (new) for regulated customers — requires security review and different pricing.
- SLAs: I’ve included the current SLOs in the doc; upgrade paths to a higher SLA are available as an add-on.

I’ll attach the proposal and the initial pricing matrix. If helpful I can schedule a 30-min call with our contracts lead next week to walk through redlines.

Best,
Sarah Lin
Enterprise Account Exec — LaunchDarkly
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract up for renewal — need detailed options

Karthik — quick notes from finance/legal after skimming Sarah’s proposal: 
- A ~10% increase for a 12-month renewal is a material step; need justification tied to clear SLO improvements or migration assistance.
- We require exportable audit logs on a weekly (preferably daily) cadence in a machine-readable format as part of the baseline; migration exports must be included without an excessive fee.
- Legal flagged indemnity, data deletion timelines, and automatic price escalators — we won’t accept unilateral increases with <90 days’ notice.

Ava/Marissa: engineering input on the on-prem option — we need to know whether the private deployment supports our existing SDKs and KV cache patterns before committing.

If we go long-term for cost, finance wants at least one cost-control mechanism (either MAU cap or predictable bucket pricing).

Laura
Head of Finance (acting)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@launchdarkly.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract up for renewal — need detailed options

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed the proposal internally and have the following counterproposal and non-negotiables: 

Counterproposal (high level):
- 36-month commit: Redwood signs a 36-month term in exchange for a 15% discount off the 36-month list price you quoted, a capped annual price increase no greater than CPI + 2%, and a 60-day notice period for any price adjustments.
- 12-month option: allow us to renew for 12 months at current list + up to 8% (instead of 10%) if 36-month is not acceptable.
- Exports & migration: production audit log exports must be available daily (JSON preferred) and a one-time full export for migration included at no extra charge.
- SLA / SLO: we need a written SLO for SDK availability and latency with defined remedies (service credits) for missed targets.
- Private deployment: if the private/VPC option is required for certain projects, we need SDK parity and clear onboarding timelines and pricing.

Attached: counter_terms_redwood_v1.docx (high-level bullet list to feed legal). Please confirm whether LaunchDarkly can accept these as a starting point. If you can’t accept the discount or the export terms, let us know exactly which items are showstoppers so we can evaluate migration risk.

Thanks — can we set a legal/ops sync for next Wed 2026-12-16 to iron out redlines?

Karthik
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@launchdarkly.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@launchdarkly.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract up for renewal — need detailed options

Karthik, Laura, team — appreciate the clear counterproposal. Quick response from our side:

- Discount: we can move to a 36-month pricing that matches a 15% effective discount if Redwood can commit to a guaranteed MAU tier and a 36-month minimum term; we’ll provide the exact tiering in the updated matrix.
- Price increases: acceptable to include a 60-day notice clause and cap increases to CPI + 2%, subject to our legal review.
- Exports: daily JSON audit exports are in scope; for the full historical export, we’ll deliver a one-time migration export (format: newline-delimited JSON) and include it as part of the professional services line-item (we can waive the service charge if committed to 36 months).
- SLA: our contracts team will draft SLO language with service credits for missed availability thresholds; we’ll aim to include this in the next draft.
- Private/VPC: roadmap says SDK parity is targeted but requires a separate security review and onboarding window (6–10 weeks).

Next steps: I’ve asked contracts to prepare an updated proposal and a DocuSign envelope for the commercial terms. Please send any redlines to contracts@launchdarkly.com. I’ve also proposed a legal sync for Wed, 2026-12-16 10:00 PT — does that work for Redwood?

Attached: LD_response_notes.txt
DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/LD-Redwood-2026
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/contacts/engagements/LD-2026-EXP-01

If the 36-month discount requires guaranteed MAU tiers we should get that spelled out; otherwise we’ll consider staged tiers during the sync.

Best,
Sarah Lin
Enterprise Account Exec — LaunchDarkly
